solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Diamonds — arranging of date, ending in ceremony –- eternally devoted?

parts.note: rocks is slang for diamonds

indicators.note: arranging signals that the letters of date are put into a new order
the ending in a word is its final letter, here of ceremony

explanation.surface: A jeweller's line about a diamond ring, a date and the end of a wedding ceremony, for a couple devoted forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging of' turns DATE into TEAD. The question mark admits the definition is a stretch: someone rock-steady never wavers, as a devoted partner should not.
explanation.definitionFit: Being utterly firm and unwavering is the idiom's sense, close to lifelong unswerving loyalty.

clue.text: Massage daily finally makes you red

parts.note: to massage is to rub

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of daily

explanation.surface: A daily massage turns your skin pink.
explanation.definitionFit: The gemstone gives its name to a deep crimson shade, so it serves as a synonym for a red colour.

clue.text: Some people do computing, picking this up

definitions.text: Some people do computing, picking this up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards
some of these words means only part of their letters are taken, spanning people do computing

explanation.surface: Some people working in computing learn programming as they go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes EDOC from the end of 'people' through the start of 'computing'; 'up' turns it round. The whole clue also describes the answer: what people in computing pick up.
explanation.definitionFit: Programming instructions are what computer workers write and learn, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Item with cachet a smutty slob's ruined

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of a smutty slob's are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A prestigious possession ruined by a grubby, foul-mouthed slob.
explanation.definitionFit: A possession owned chiefly to show off one's wealth or rank carries cachet, meaning prestige.

clue.text: Reprimand, and what it may make you, if not at first

indicators.note: if not at first says the opening letter is dropped from the word just found

parts.note: a reprimand may leave you frightened, that is fearful

explanation.surface: A telling-off, and how it might leave you feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle phrase refers back to the reprimand: a scolding can make you FEARFUL; 'if not at first' drops its F.
explanation.definitionFit: An earful is an informal word for a long scolding, the sense of a sharp reprimand.

clue.text: Vehicle in view, heading off and moving up in driving contest

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving up means the whole thing is read from bottom to top
in puts the vehicle inside the shortened word for view
heading off says the first letter is removed from the word for view

parts.note: to view something is to regard it
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car comes into sight, turns off and climbs, as in a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves EGARD; 'moving up' reads the whole assembly, ECARGARD, from the bottom of this down light. A drag race is a sprint between two cars from a standing start.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprint between cars over a short straight track is a competitive motoring event, so it is a contest of driving.

clue.text: Try to eradicate a black plant

indicators.note: to eradicate means the letter a is wiped out of the word for try

parts.note: a judge tries, or hears, a case
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An attempt to kill off a black weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is a legal sense: to HEAR a case. 'to eradicate' removes its A, leaving HER.
explanation.definitionFit: Any small non-woody flowering plant, or one used for flavour, is a herb, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Detective with careful approach securing prisoner's appearance of trust?

indicators.note: securing means the two pieces hold the prisoner between them

parts.note: a private eye is a detective
tact is a careful, diplomatic approach
con is short for convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A detective's tactful interrogation of a prisoner, aimed at winning trust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' places CON at the join of EYE and TACT. The question mark marks the definition as loose: meeting someone's gaze suggests honesty.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking someone in the eye conveys sincerity, so meeting their gaze looks like trustworthiness.

clue.text: Labour upset American business support

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the abbreviation is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Lab is the usual abbreviation for the British Labour Party
US stands for American, as in United States
trade is business or commerce

explanation.surface: The Labour Party is annoyed at American firms backing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of small posts holding up a handrail is a supporting structure on a staircase or balcony.

clue.text: A shocking time, in terms of shock?

definitions.text: A shocking time, in terms of shock?

parts.words: A shocking time, in terms of shock?
parts.note: a shock is also a thick mass of hair, so a day when it looks awful is a shocking time for your shock

explanation.surface: A traumatic experience described in terms of the trauma itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' means a mop of hair as well as a fright: a day when your hair won't behave, and the phrase for a day when everything goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a day when one's hair is unmanageable, and by extension any day of frustration and setbacks.

clue.text: Go out, avoiding sun — coming back, suffer effects of sun?

indicators.note: coming back means the remaining letters are read in reverse
avoiding means the word for go out does without the abbreviation for sun

parts.note: to go out like a light is to fall asleep, so go out is to sleep
S is short for sun, as in Sun. for Sunday

explanation.surface: Someone stays indoors out of the sun, then comes back sunburnt anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' takes S from SLEEP, leaving LEEP; 'coming back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunburnt skin flakes away in strips, so shedding skin is a familiar result of too much sunshine.

clue.text: Ranting to baffle Catholic congregation

parts.note: to stump someone is to baffle them
the Oratory is a Catholic congregation of priests founded by St Philip Neri

explanation.surface: A sermon designed to bewilder a Catholic congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: The name recalls politicians speaking from a tree stump; the definition is a noun, as 'ranting' can be.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud, emotive speechmaking of the soapbox kind is ranting, a noun for impassioned harangues.

clue.text: Court dismissing last two tribunals after review and lots of study

indicators.note: after review means the remaining letters together with tribunals are looked over again and reordered
dismissing last two means the final pair of letters of court are thrown out

explanation.surface: A court rejects two final tribunal decisions after an appeal, following much study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing last two' leaves COU, which joins the tribunals in one pool before 'after review' rearranges them. The answer is a rare word for night-time study by lamplight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means laborious study or the writings from it, especially work done late at night, so it is plural study.

clue.text: Say dealing in currency's substantial

parts.note: forex is short for foreign exchange, trade in currencies
ample means plentiful, substantial

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that currency dealing is a big business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like a verb; it is the 'say' that introduces an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Say, used before an instance, is a synonym for the phrase introducing an illustration, as in 'take a city, say Paris'.

clue.text: Notice haulier's under municipal feature

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the haulier below the word for notice

parts.note: to clock something is slang for noticing it
a tower is one who tows, a haulier; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A sign reading that the haulage firm is beneath the town hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haulier's' reads as 'haulier is'; TOWER here rhymes with 'mower', someone who tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall structure with a large timepiece is a classic civic landmark on a town hall or square.

clue.text: Blinking line I exhibit when cycling?

indicators.note: when cycling means letters are moved round from the front to the back

parts.note: to exhibit is to show

explanation.surface: A cyclist's blinking light, displayed while riding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when cycling' moves L and I from the front of LISHOW to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl seems to blink solemnly through big eyes, so a blinking, bespectacled look is described as like an owl.

clue.text: Ape, losing head, stepping back, cracking principal weapon

indicators.note: cracking means the reversed letters break into the word for principal

parts.note: a star is the principal performer

indicators.note: stepping back means what remains is read in reverse
losing head means the first letter of the word for ape is dropped

parts.note: to ape is to mimic

explanation.surface: A beheaded ape retreats and splits open the head's weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' is the verb, to imitate, not the animal. 'losing head' leaves IMIC and 'stepping back' turns that to CIMI before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved single-edged sword of Middle Eastern origin is a classic bladed weapon.

clue.text: Food? Fruit split has one tucking in

parts.note: a nut is a fruit

indicators.note: tucking in means the numeral is tucked inside the word for split

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A split fruit with something tucked inside, served as food.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that nourishes the body is nourishment, and the question mark admits food is a loose fit.

clue.text: Naughty once, with mother restricting one's praise

indicators.note: naughty means the letters of once misbehave and come out jumbled
restricting means the word for mother hems in the numeral

parts.note: mum is mother
I is the Roman numeral for one; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A child once naughty, kept in check by mum, now earns praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' gives ENCO and 'restricting' gives MIUM. The 's of 'one's' reads as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech or text of high praise is a eulogy or tribute, so the word means praise.

clue.text: Required US industrialist to accommodate church

indicators.note: to accommodate means the industrialist's name gives room to the church abbreviation

parts.note: Henry Ford was the American car maker
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: An American magnate was obliged to house a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Being compelled or made obligatory is the sense: something forced on you is required of you.

clue.text: Running costs continue, after switching components

indicators.note: after switching components means the two parts of the phrase swap places

parts.note: to keep up is to continue

explanation.surface: Operating expenses keep rising after parts are replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after switching components' swaps KEEP and UP.
explanation.definitionFit: The cost of maintaining something in good order is the regular outlay for its running.

clue.text: Second chance to view translation of poetical yarn

indicators.note: a translation renders words in other terms, here poetical yarn reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A translated epic poem gives readers another chance to see the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Television replays a key sporting moment so viewers can see it once more, a second look at the event.

clue.text: Talent? Minimum of talent linked to moving image

parts.note: a GIF is a short animated image file

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is its smallest part, its first letter, here of talent

explanation.surface: Even a little talent linked to animation is a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural ability or flair is a synonym for an inborn knack.

clue.text: Escape's a narrow thing

definitions.meaning: to give someone the ... is to escape from them
a slender strip, as of paper or land, is a narrow thing

explanation.surface: A getaway that was a close-run affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard synonyms: to slide away from captors, and a small thin strip of something.

clue.text: Man's son abandoning eggs

indicators.note: abandoning means the word for eggs leaves out the abbreviation for son

parts.note: spawn is the eggs of fish or frogs

explanation.surface: A man's son walking out on the family nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess sense: the pieces are called men.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces are called men, and the lowliest of them is the foot soldier on the front row.

clue.text: Ritual representing one miracle

indicators.note: representing means the letters of one miracle are presented again in a new order

explanation.surface: A rite depicting a single miracle.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal and solemn observance is ritual, and the word is both an adjective and a noun for a rite.

clue.text: Secure note provided by musical sense

indicators.note: provided by puts the note after the musical sense

parts.note: an ear for music is a musical sense
n. is an abbreviation for note, as in a footnote reference

explanation.surface: A musician gets a note right thanks to a good ear.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure a wage or prize is to gain it by effort, a synonym for obtaining it through work.

clue.text: Flight arrangement done in stages

definitions.meaning: a flight of stairs is arranged as one tread after another
proceeding gradually, one move at a time

explanation.surface: An airline itinerary planned leg by leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes stairs laid out tread after tread and, figuratively, anything done gradually.
